description: RHD Labs is a Toronto-based solo team building an open-source project to make NASA NISAR radar data easier to explore and understand. The project brings together geospatial data, Python/PostGIS, and clear visual storytelling. I’m currently participating solo.
summary: RHD Labs explores how NASA–ISRO NISAR radar can make surface change easier to understand. Our interactive prototype presents Saskatchewan agricultural-moisture and British Columbia slope-change scenarios, a windowed-data/PostGIS architecture, and a captioned concept reel. All scenario imagery and readings are explicitly simulated, not validated NISAR detections or operational warnings.
details:
RHD Labs proposes an inspectable path from NISAR radar products to an understandable view of surface change: discover suitable GCOV observations through NASA Earthdata/ASF; read a bounding-box window through a supported HDF5 transport using earthaccess and h5py; compare compatible observations; index validated geographic features and provenance in PostgreSQL/PostGIS; and serve GeoJSON through FastAPI to a CesiumJS cockpit based on gods-eye-view.

This initial submission delivers an interactive public showcase, two synthetic Canadian scenarios, a comparison slider, an architecture walkthrough, a 28.8-second English-captioned concept reel, a seven-slide presentation, and an Apache-2.0 Python/PostGIS foundation.

All displayed moisture percentages, displacement readings, change imagery, and structure counts are simulated examples. No NISAR granule has been analyzed by this showcase. GCOV backscatter alone does not establish soil saturation or water depth; GUNW displacement is relative along the radar line of sight and requires further interpretation and validation. The scenarios are not emergency warnings.

Live HDF5 ingestion, quantitative change analysis, and the full 3D/voice cockpit are separate application integrations and are not claimed as validated in this initial submission.

The full Apache-2.0 source package is downloadable directly from the public showcase while the GitHub mirror remains pending:

https://rhd-labs-dancing-with-the-sars.winnieintheweeds.chatgpt.site/assets/project-source.zip

Use of SI: Google Gemini supplied the initial outline. OpenAI/Codex assisted with the delivered code, documentation, presentation, captions, procedural visuals, and synthesized ambient audio. Claude/Fable was assigned separate application work; its integration is not verified in this submission snapshot. SI-assisted content is identified in the public project and its metadata. No ElevenLabs/Higgsfield-generated narration or B-roll is included. All scenario readings are synthetic.
